svg.aria-label: The four DHCP messages, discover, offer, request and acknowledge, followed by a renewal half-way through the lease

g.text: plus mask, router, name server, 24 hours
still broadcast: other servers learn they lost
12 hours later: straight to the server

ol.li: Discover. Alice’s laptop has no address, and doesn’t know who to ask, so it sends from 0.0.0.0 to the broadcast address 255.255.255.255, UDP port 67.
Offer. Any DHCP server that hears it offers an address from its pool, with everything else the laptop needs: the netmask, the router, the name server, and how long it can keep them.
Request. The laptop accepts one offer, and says so to everyone, so that any other server that made an offer knows it wasn’t chosen.
Acknowledge. The server confirms. The laptop checks that nobody else is using the address (the ARP probe from Chapter 21), and it’s online.

The address is only leased. Half-way through, the laptop asks the same server, directly this time, to renew it. If that server is gone, it tries anyone at 87.5%, and when the lease runs out it must stop using the address.
